candidates.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
candidates.content: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmar

candidates.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
candidates.content: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress. We introduce Re-Search, which adapts the format of Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only the research problem of a published paper, a model must rediscover the paper's core idea by asking yes-or-no questions. Built from 200 ICML 2026 papers, Re-Search tracks how a model's idea evolves as it asks questions and receives binary oracle feedback, isolating ideation from execution. Across six recent LLMs, nearly all progress happens within the first 30 of 100 questions, which largely decide how the game ends; after that, most models plateau. Through controlled interventions on the candidate questions and the hypothesis space, we find that the bottleneck is generation, not judgment: models recognize a good idea or a good question when one is offered, but often cannot produce it on their own. We further analyze the ideation traces and find that models fail by either over-exploiting one direction or over-exploring too many.

candidates.title: Dual Flow: Joint Image-Measurement Interpolation for Inverse Problems
candidates.content: Generative model-based approaches to linear inverse problems typically use the acquired noisy measurement to condition or guide sampling in the image domain. In this work, we introduce Dual Flow, a novel joint-flow model for solving linear inverse problems by jointly estimating the clean image and corresponding noise-free measurement from the observation. Specifically, Dual Flow formulates image reconstruction and measurement denoising as a coupled estimation problem, using coupled flows in the image and measurement domains. The acquired noisy measurement is used only to initialize the measurement state; thereafter, image and measurement states are jointly updated based on their current values. By construction, the final image and measurement estimates are guaranteed to satisfy the underlying forward model. We derive the sampling updates for the joint-flow which involves the conditional mean of the clean image given the joint state. We further derive a closed-form expression for a sufficient statistic of the joint state and show that the required conditional mean can be obtained by solving an image-domain Gaussian denoising problem involving operator-dependent, correlated noise. candidates.title: Minimal, synthetic arginine deiminase pathway provides full ATP demand for cellular growth
candidates.content: Bottom-up construction of synthetic cells requires a simple, yet robust ATP-generating system. The arginine deiminase (ADI) pathway offers a minimal, enzyme-based alternative to more complex ATP-producing systems such as glycolytic routes, respiratory chains or photosystems. Here, we implement the ADI pathway in Escherichia coli and test its capacity to fully replace native ATP generation. First, we designed and tested synthetic ADI operons through combinatorial library screening and selected high-performing variants. Using the best performing-ADI variant, we progressively reduced the cells dependence on native ATP generation while increasing selection for ADI-dependent growth through targeted knockout strains and growth conditions, followed by adaptive laboratory evolution. This resulted in a strain in which the ADI pathway sustained growth in minimal medium at a doubling time of 21 hours, serving as the sole source of ATP. Whole-genome sequencing of evolved strains revealed that this transition required loss-of-function mutations in the native respiratory chain. candidates.title: Web-Based Training for Pain Management
candidates.content: [NA] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: Lokman Hekim University | 适应症: Pain Management. Inadequate management of pain during vaccination may lead to negative vaccination experiences, needle fear, and future vaccine non-adherence in children. This study aims to develop a web-based pain management education program for nurses/midwives and parents to reduce vaccination-related pain in children and evaluate its effectiveness. The study will be conducted using a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with a non-randomized control group in two Family Health Centers. Pain will be assessed using the FLACC Pain Scale for children aged 0-3 years and the Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale for children aged 3 years and older. Pain management practices will be evaluated using an observation form. The information quality of the program will be assessed using DISCERN, and its usability will be evaluated using the System Usability Scale (SUS). Data will be analyzed using appropriate parametric and non-parametric tests. The intervention effect will be evaluated by examining the group-by-time interaction. Statistical significance will be set at p\<0.05.

candidates.title: SWIFT: Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning of Time-Series Foundation Models for Forecasting
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.17915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While current few-shot adaptation strategies for time series forecasting foundation models are predominantly dataset-centric, the necessity of obtaining an additional dataset for the finetuning process poses a significant hurdle for adoption. To address this constraint, we propose Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning (SWIFT), a novel forecasting adaptation framework that achieves fine-grained specialization by leveraging structural priors from the target instance's own history. This shift allows the fine-tuning process to be entirely transparent to the end-user, which significantly enhances the ease of adoption. To implement this framework, SWIFT synergizes Self-Retrieval for historical mining and Frequency-Aware Loss for spectral consistency, while employing Deviation-Aware Dynamic Fusion to balance adaptation with general knowledge preservation. Extensive experiments across four TSFM backbones and three long-history benchmark subsets validate SWIFT, yielding average MASE and WQL reductions of 6.41% and 4.83% across 24 combinations of four backbones and six Chronos Benchmark II datasets. candidates.title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States
candidates.content: arXiv:2611.18272v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing memory forensics for machine learning systems typically targets static artifacts, such as model weights or prompt logs, rather than the transient computational states of a live inference process. This gap limits an examiner's ability to analyze the specific behavior of a running large language model (LLM) service that cannot be restarted or modified. We present a method for acquiring per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU process using a non-modifying debugger, without requiring prior knowledge of the model's architecture parameters or weights. The approach employs a general six-stage process with platform-specific adapters, utilizing either a PyTorch allocator clock or a kernel-launch clock to identify and read tensor allocations from video memory. We validate this acquisition on 33 open-source decoder-only models across nine architecture classes, demonstrating that the recovered bytes are byte-exact and usable for downstream analysis. As a use case, we apply linear probes trained on standard framework activations to the recovered states, successfully distinguishing refusal from compliance with an AUROC of 0
